#4040. Airframe Ultra's PS1 cyberpunk city is an amazing tribute to G-Police and WipEout, and I wish you people would slow down to appreciate it

But what if we could gawk at the dumpsters

I do not wish to "rule the streets" of Megacity West, dear creators of Airframe Ultra. I wish to be ravished by them, rubbing my face against the rusty corrugated metal of the shipping containers, and savouring the acid blue waters of the bay. I do not want to "become the one thing with freedom in a city of billions: A racer." I want to become the other thing with freedom in a city of billions: a person who slowly drives or – whisper it - walks around just looking at stuff, because gadzooks, this is one of the prettiest PS1 cyberpunk burgs I've laid eyes on.

Those eroded pastel chevrons. Those seductively wobbling vertices. That electric reef of a downtown backdrop, murderously luring your gaze from the on-coming trucks. That layer of invigorating crackle over everything. Every moment or so, I dismount from my hoverbike to inspect some concrete ruin I could swear I last saw in G-Police, or ponder the resemblance between a subway tunnel and WipEout 2097's Gare d'Europa. Then, somebody waps me in the skull with a stop sign at 300 kilometres an hour. But I was already stopped, frantic stranger! Your brutal poetic ironies are wasted on me.

Despite my best efforts, Airframe Ultra is a battle racer. It's co-developed by Videocult, the people behind Rain World – a game it looks nothing like, but is comparable to in the sense that there is an ocean of industrial refuse to navigate, and you will very often die. Each battle race is broken into sprints around a branching course that has been smashed together by the forces of urban decay. You will corkscrew down storm drains and barge through old abandoned clifftop mansions under a scarlet sun, zip along deadly flyovers and thread the barely legible layouts of high density slums.

Your hoverbike handles like a bronco full of helium, and that's before you start wanging it off the gloriously marbled, low-poly rubbish heaps that stud the city, shunting the game's camera through surfaces and exposing the map's underside in what the absolute squares amongst my readers will doubtless deem "an inelegance", but which true turbojunkeys will appreciate for its makeshift exuberance.

You've got a boost button which generally gets you exploded – and all that's before you get to the time-limited battle arenas that bookend each sprint. Here, players attempt to slaughter each other as much as possible, spending collectible cash on floating weapon pick-ups that range from bent pipes to Gatling guns and EMP grenades. Then it's off for another sprint. The first player to earn 10 points and place first in a subsequent sprint wins the match. I have not won many matches. My primary goal right now in Airframe Ultra is persuading everybody to stop and swap some emotes, while I coo over an amazing piece of graffiti I've found.

My efforts to make Airframe Ultra a walking sim aren't just about scenery. The game is surprisingly engrossing on foot, with some woozy tank controls that make me think of the experimental days before every third-person control scheme became a variation on Assassin's Creed, Uncharted or Gears of War. You have to hammer a button to run, for instance, and you'll wind yourself fast. You can also perform punches and kicks in four directions, with grander attacks to discover by smooshing together inputs. You'd best believe I burst into tears when I realised what this reminded me of: it's Bungie's Oni! The game with the finest martial arts system ever coded! There are more obvious influences, like Road Rash, but in these grim days of endless parrying, I'll take all the Konoko callbacks I can get.

Ahhhhh. But if only this had a proper single player mode. Online and local splitscreen with drop-in bot support are all you get. I wouldn't say Airframe is the most balanced deathracer, either. In my experience, and do bear in mind I mostly try to avoid the racing component, victory typically goes to whoever lands a fat cash reserve and grabs an AK47. That mild shambolicness is arguably part of the charm, in that it supplies incentive to stop and drink in the atmosphere. These streets are big and broken and beautiful enough for all of us, friends. Let us rule them together. Read more on Steam.

#4039. Base PS5's QSSR Enhancer Coming to 6 More Games, in Spider-Man 2 Now

Control Resonant, Arc Raiders, and more upgraded

Sony has announced it is expanding support for its QSSR graphics enhancer on base PS5 to six more PS5 games in the coming weeks.

Through a free update, the feature is live right now in Marvel's Spider-Man 2. In addition, the following titles will receive support for QSSR soon:

More games will receive QSSR support in the future too, as Sony continues to work with developers in implementing the visual enhancement technology. "Developers are just getting started," Sony states. with the PS5 Pro has had PSSR since launch, which was recently upgraded via new version, the QSSR tech is designed for the base PS5 system.

Ghost of Yotei and Marvel's Wolverine also support the feature.

News Sony Confirms Refined Version of Acclaimed PSSR Upscaler for Base PS5, with 'Remarkable' Potential

"It's great to be improving the PS5 this far into the generation"

QSSR support in Marvel's Spider-Man 2 is live now, and head of technology at Insomniac Games, Mike Fitzgerald, told the PlayStation Blog you should spot improved image stability and sharpness across both the Fidelity and Performance modes in the game.

Remedy expects to have QSSR support added to Control Resonant in December, at which point the PS5 title will have a "more stable and detailed image". Here's a comparison video:

Embark Studios is supporting QSSR across both its multiplayer games, The Finals and Arc Raiders. Once the PS5 patch is applied, expect "increased sharpness, better environmental clarity and overall visual improvements". Here is another comparison video for Arc Raiders specifically:

When No Man's Sky is updated with QSSR support, it'll "render the universe in sharper, cleaner and more beautiful detail, while delivering the best possible framerate". The patch should become available in the next few weeks.

#4038. Terrific fantasy RPG Queen's Domain gets first proper update, adding a new throwing weapon and options to make puzzles "less frustrating"

Extremely good King's Field-style RPG Queen's Domain – or is it a Metroid Prime homage? Or a stealth Morrowind-up? We hacks simply cannot decide – has received its first proper patch, adding a hitherto "missing" throwing weapon, the Grave Knife, alongside a bunch of quality-of-life fixes.

They've stirred in the ability to disable screenshake, alongside some new icons to make status effects more obvious. They've also introduced "options to make some late game puzzles less frustrating", though they don't specify which. How frustrating! Still, it's a tidy overhaul for a game that has rapidly become one of my 2026 favourites.

The big mystery with the update is what the new Grave Knife does. You'll find it inside the Tower of Knowledge, once you've managed to unlock passage. As for those overly aggravating late game puzzles – I find the toughest part of puzzling in Queen's Domain is often just spotting switches and key objects, so perhaps it's something to do with that?

True, there's a large selection of skeleton tableaus who comically point the way to your next objectives, but the game's pixel aesthetics can be rather dense. I very much approve of this on the whole. I like how organic and tumbledown the environment feels - the repeated delight of realising that, yes, you can get over there, and wow, there's a whole other level down here.

Queen's Domain has earned a lot of happy reactions, and is a solid commercial hit. Developers Freshly Baked say it has sold over 100,000 copies, with Vertical Slice reporting that they've already broken even. Glad tidings indeed. Find the full patch notes below, via Steam.

#4034. I just found out you can use your Steam Wishlist to search for deals on games outside of Steam, saving my nephew more than £40 on Total War: Warhammer 3

It earned me a bucketload of uncle points

I may be very late to the party with this discovery, but I only just realised you can connect your Steam Wishlist to a third-party deals tracker. The beauty of which is that, once hooked up, you can see what games you've been pining for are going cheap not just on Steam but through any major shopfront across the internet.

I worry that I will be coming across as 'Use this one trick to save money – greengrocers hate it!', but it's already helped save my nephew more than £40. Even if it meant using a slightly underhand method.

Two weeks ago, I got a text from my nephew asking what the best way to play Total War: Warhammer 3. When I messaged back a couple of hours later (look, I'm not a responsive uncle) to tell him it's currently £50 on Steam, but it's worth waiting because according to SteamDB's price history it's come down to £7.50 in the past, I was too late. He'd got itchy feet and bought it at full whack on Steam, using up all his birthday money.

That's when I went looking and found Is There Any Deal for the first time. (A lot of you in the comments may be throwing your hands up in despair to hear this oversight) If you've not come across it before, it's a site that tracks game sales across loads of shops, including Steam, EA Store, Epic Games Store, GamersGate, GOG. GreenManGaming, Humble. This means while a game may not be on sale on Steam you can see if it's on sale anywhere else.

In the case of Total War: Warhammer 3, while it was full price on Steam, over on the Humble Store it was discounted to £7.49. I sent a link to my nephew and then told him, using the authority only an uncle has, that it's okay to refund the game through Steam and buy the cheaper version. It's not something I've ever done myself, but he's 17 and that is a lot of money to save.

Anyway, that's recommendation the first. It was only when I was looking for a way to export my Steam Wishlist to ask RPS supporters what I should cull that I realised Is There Any Deal has another feature: you can import every game on your Wishlist to get deal notifications. (This may get a second groan of despair in the comment section.) Once linked up, the site will ping you a notification whenever games you're waiting for pop up in a deal.

Just looking at my current list, I can get Genesis Noir, Ancient Enemy, and Norco for £10 total, all of which with more than 70% discounts through stores other than Steam. So, as you can see, this could be both a saving technically and lead me to spending a lot more money than I mean to…

You may already have heard of these tools, but as I hadn't I thought it best to give them a shout out.

Now considering I've revealed myself to be a rube, what other third party tools should I be installing to weaponise my Steam Library?

#4033. Real-time strategy game The Fertile Crescent 2 is an isometric odyssey inspired by Age of Empires, with the 1.0 release out now

Time to power-rank the biggest Bronze Age civs

Age of Empires-influenced real-time strategy game The Fertile Crescent 2: Collapse of the Bronze Age leaves early access today, publishers MicroProse have announced, with the 1.0 version adding the final chapters of the singleplayer story. You'll also get your grubby fingers on the very same map editor developers Wield Interactive used to design the campaign.

I'm new to The Fertile Crescent 2 myself. I do like the sound of a strategy sim in which you guide a fugitive community through the Late Bronze Age Collapse. The land has been thrown into turmoil by the arrival of the Sea People, this being a loose historical term for assorted ocean-going migrants who, I gather, are often blamed for the crumbling of the Hittites among other once-glorious Bronze Age powers. I don't have much scholarly insight to share - I thought the "Sea People" referred to expansionist mermaids, at first - but I do have a trailer.

Nate Crowley (RPS in peace) was exceedingly fond of the original game, calling it "a bite-sized chunk of phenomenal RTS design" that "manages to riff nostalgically on Age Of Empires, while completely rewriting its ground rules". The sequel continues with the same core concepts – above all, the paramount importance of food, which determines population and army size together with your civ's progression.

"This is not a game about building the biggest empire," the developers explain in a press release. "Resources have to be managed, stability is fragile, and growth comes with risk. Every expansion, every battle, and every decision must be weighed against survival. Building and managing a sustainable economy is as important as commanding your forces in battle. Expanding your army too quickly can put your food economy under pressure."

The story spans 17 missions, with four playable factions: the Assyrians, Egyptians, Babylonians, and Hittites. The 1.0 release also includes some standalone scenario missions, a skirmish mode, and multiplayer on dedicated servers with bot support.

Read more on Steam. If you're partial to historical strategy and don't mind winding back the clock (upturning the hourglass? Adjusting the sundial? Recalibrating the henge?) another few thousand years, Folk Emerging is pretty terrific. If you like stories about migrant tribes, and you don't mind trading your Hittites for Vikings, you might get a kick out of The Banner Saga.

#4031. GTA 6's In-Game Animated TV Series, Macca & Friends, Hints at the Game's Absurd Scope

I think this might be the one thing about GTA 6 that's really made me aware of the sheer scale of what Rockstar Games is cooking up.

Exclusively revealed via DiscussingFilm, an in-game, animated TV series named Macca & Friends has been revealed with the below teaser trailer:

What strikes me about this is that the show looks exactly like the sort of thing you would see on Adult Swim. It has similar vibes to other cartoons aimed at adults, like Aqua Teen Hunger Force or Rick & Morty.

What I mean is, this doesn't look like your typical throwaway gag that plays on a loop in the background. It looks like a full production on its own.

It's described as a "series" in the official blurb, so it seems this will have multiple episodes you can watch within GTA 6. The show "follows the adventures of Macca the Gator and his wetland friends across the state of Leonida."

This won't be the only thing you can tune into, either; according to Kinda Funny, there are multiple shows that have been created, including a "novela" and another animated show called The Johnsons.

They say Rockstar "hired an animation studio" to create these things, and that seemingly includes Macca & Friends.

If this is the sort of scope we can expect from just watching TV in GTA 6, it gets me excited about the level of detail and scope in the rest of the game.

#4030. DOOM: The Dark Ages DLC ‘Revelations’ – ‘Slaughter Mode’ update launches November 16

Publisher Bethesda Softworks and developer id Software will release a free update for DOOM: The Dark Ages paid downloadable content “Revelations” on November 16 that adds the endless combat mode, “Slaughter Mode,” the companies announced.

Push your slaying skills to the limit with Slaughter Mode, a new endless combat challenge available November 16 as a free update for owners of DOOM: The Dark Ages downloadable content “Revelations.”

Tear through relentless, escalating and unpredictable waves of demonic hordes, carving out your personal best scores and unlocking rewards using the Skulls collected from the carnage. With each checkpoint reached, players must ask themselves if they want to cash in their run or risk it all for more slaughter.

No two runs through Slaughter Mode are identical as you fight escalating rounds of random encounters, bosses and arenas, turning up the heat as you proceed further into your run.

Complete rounds to earn Skulls, which unlock rewards such as Slaughter Mode-only Slayer skins, weapon skins for all modes and profile icons. You can also unlock tracks from Andrew Hulshult’s IDKFA soundtrack to play in both Slaughter Mode and the Ripatorium! Take on weekly challenges for more opportunities to earn rewards and show off your slaying prowess.

Survive long enough to reach a Round Checkpoint and you’ll have the chance to Secure your current Skulls against death. Choose Risk It instead to add to your Skull Multiplier, increasing the Skulls you can earn during the run—but there’s a catch. If you’re slain while Risk It is active, all your unsecured Skulls are forfeited!

Death isn’t the end, however: every Round Checkpoint you complete also unlocks another starting point for future runs, letting you resume the carnage in those later encounters sooner.

DOOM: The Dark Ages is available now for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, and PC via Steam and Microsoft Store. It is also available via Game Pass.

#4028. PSA: Xbox And GTA 6 Have Both Pushed Out Small New Updates

One's a console update, the other potentially a "day one" patch

As we get ready to wrap up the working week here at Pure Xbox, we wanted to alert you to a couple of new updates that have been pushed out in recent days - one for Xbox consoles in general, and another specifically for GTA 6.

The Xbox console update was actually released on Wednesday, but nobody made a song and dance about it whatsoever, while the patch notes only referenced "general stability and performance improvements".

However, we now know that the update was related to the addition of achievements in four original Xbox games, and unless you download the update, you won't be able to see those achievements right now.

There's a chance your console may have downloaded this automatically but to check, go to "Settings", "System", "Updates" and then see if there's an update waiting to be downloaded or not.

News Four OG Xbox Games Are Getting Achievements For The First Time Ever

"We’re introducing one of the top requested features"

As for GTA 6, in addition to the 200GB+ preload that went live a few days ago, there's also now a new update as of a few hours ago that sits at around 2.2GB. You'll need to download this in order to start playing on November 19th.

Some people are speculating that this might be the so-called "day one patch", but who knows whether we might get another one between now and next Thursday. In any case, you'll want to get this queued up as soon as possible (unless you haven't installed the game yet, in which case it'll be included in your initial download).

There's a chance you may see a different size, but it's somewhere around that 2.2GB mark. We're also spotting that some people haven't got it yet for whatever reason, but it should roll out to all Xbox users in the very near future.

Don't forget that Alpha Skip-Ahead Xbox Insiders have also received a special new update this week that adds three new features for testing purposes, so if you're part of the Insider programme, keep an eye out for that.

#4027. After Star Wars Zero Company dev Bit Reactor brought back an unspecified number of furloughed devs, some of those who weren't have seemingly been laid off

"I’m really proud of what we built together"

Early last month, Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor brought back a number of developers who had been furloughed before the game launched in August. At the time they did not specify how many devs were returning to the studio, with a separate report claiming more than half had become full time staffers again. Unfortunately, it does now seem like not everyone was able to be brought back, with a number of now former workers sharing word of having been laid off.

As spotted by Star Wars outlet Bespin Bulletin, multiple developers shared word of their layoffs to LinkedIn. A producer at Bit Reactor, Michael Blackard was seemingly one of the first to report being laid off, alongside senior QA analyst Ryan Mosher. Ryan Lopez, an environment artist at the studio, shared, "I was laid off from Bit Reactor this week after a three-month furlough, and while it stings, I’m really proud of what we built together." Lopez had apparently been working on the game for more than three years, starting all the way back on the game's pre-production period.

Tyler Eichten, a UI engineer, also said, "As of today, my time with Bit Reactor has come to a close due to a layoff. I am immensely proud of the work that I, the UI/UX team, and the team at large have accomplished. I hope that in this tumultuous industry that my coworkers (and myself) find placement." It's unclear at this point in time if any, or how many, other staffers have been formally laid off, and Bit Reactor are yet to make a comment.

Star Wars Zero Company performed very well both critically and commercially, making it all the more disappointing that not all of those who worked on the game, who made it as great as it seemingly is, get to continue working at the studio. As always, solidarity with all devs affected.

#4024. "I feel that sense of responsibility more acutely": After BioWare's closure, the makers of a new Mass Effect 3 co-op remaster mod look to carry their legacy

"It's like watching a friend lose a parent - maybe you're not attached, but you feel the secondhand distress"

It appears I was premature in suggesting that the closure of BioWare might quickly spell an end for Mass Effect 3's strangely good, preposterously enduring co-op mode. I reinstalled and logged on just last week, and easily found a series of packed lobbies. Still, it was always regrettable that 2021's Mass Effect Legendary Edition opted not to remaster this multiplayer component alongside its dolled-up main trilogy, thus failing to introduce to a new generation the joys of performing teleporting psychic headbutts as a millennia-old bipedal frog.

This oversight has now been addressed, with the release of the Legendary Edition Multiplayer mod for said remaster. It's both a reconstruction and a slight expansion of ME3 multi, built in secret since 2023 by the ME3Tweaks group: a modding collective who've previously imbued the Legendary Edition with Mass Effect 1's Pinnacle Station DLC. It's also, some of its makers tell me, a bittersweet expression of appreciation for a series that looks unlikely to continue after EA's Mass Effect 5 cancellation.

At least some of that affection can be seen in how Legendary Edition Multiplayer differs from the already-available LEMP mod, which uses AI vibecoding to slap a mechanically identical recreation of ME3's co-op into the Legendary Edition's ones and zeroes. ME3Tweaks's version instead adds, according to member and longtime ME modder Audemus, a "completely overhauled UI, rebaked level lighting, upscaled and redrawn textures, upgraded shaders, native LE features such as HDR and controller support, networking and server replication improvements, extensive bug fixes, and entirely new wave modes such as Unified and Coalition."

Unified mode, for instance, quite literally mixes up ME3's enemy factions by forming mishmashed waves of baddies from across the Geth, Reaper, and Cerberus armies, thereby dusting off and stamping on your 14-year-old battle tactics. The mod also offers the ability to use ME3Tweaks' own servers for matchmaking, though a private server option remains for scraps with mates.

I'll definitely be giving this a try, once I'm back from my current travels. Though as with those OG ME3 multiplayer sessions last week, it'll be with a certain glumness, knowing that – despite a vocal campaign to give Mass Effect 5 a reprieve– I'll be playing something that had its future cut short.

The circumstances aren't lost on Legendary Edition Multiplayer's creators. "BioWare's closure is an incredibly sad moment for the games industry, and a particularly heartbreaking thing for the Mass Effect fanbase to contend with," Audemus tells me over email. "I feel as though our responsibility as a modding community has always been to carry the torch for this franchise, with or without an official future for it. But now that the future of Mass Effect has never been more in question, I feel that sense of responsibility more acutely than I ever have before."

Mgamerz, another modder on the project, recalls how "The day BioWare closed it didn't hit me until later in the day, a sort of numbness I can't really describe. I've spent 14 years working on their games - it's like watching a friend lose a parent - maybe you're not attached, but you feel the secondhand distress."

For some Legendary Edition Multiplayer modders, the affected BioWare staff included developers they knew personally. ME3Tweaks had previously been invited to embargoed discussions with both BioWare and EA on game modding, and Mass Effect writer and director Mac Walters (who left BioWare voluntarily in 2023) allegedly advocated for an even closer relationship.

"It's a shame to see it shut down," Mgamerz says. "Everyone speculated about it, but I know from talking to people internally there, that nobody knew the guillotine was about to drop." [Owners EA say the decision was only made after "months of planning, review, and analysis", though independent reporting suggests it was largely down to a straight choice between making ME5 or Star Wars Battlefront 3.]

"When we had our NDA with BioWare (since expired), apparently Mac Walters pushed internally to get my dev team brought into the manifold," he adds. "I say this as 'apparently', cause due to scheduling issues we never got to speak with Mac. But secondhand stories tell me he was a big proponent of modders - something that I would have loved to see more publicly shown.

"It is disappointing to know that the people who helped build the world my work now builds upon were killed unceremoniously - a problem that plagues the industry, and what kept me from further pursuing entry into it, something I used to dream of doing when I was younger."

RPS lawyers are telling me to tell you that nobody was literally killed. All the same, and even as someone much more familiar with playing the Mass Effects than tinkering around in their engine bays, the ME3Tweaks team make relatable points: we can frolick around an uprezzed Firebase Hydro, biotically biffing half-robot Turians like it's 2012, but it'll be hard not to look at all those conspicuous waist-high walls and think about the people who put them there. The same's true of having your mind drift to thoughts of their successors.

But there's another way of looking at it, which is that mods like Legendary Edition Multiplayer can preserve and maintain an original developer's work well beyond what their leveraged-buyout executive overlords might deem financially inconvenient. "I hope," as Audemus puts it, "that this mod - along with the fact that we've been able to build the technology to make mods like this in the first place - sends a message that there is incredible value in this franchise, and a passionate fanbase that is not ready to say goodbye to this universe and these games."

#4023. God of War: Sons of Sparta Really Will Be Ported Backwards to PS4

Out on 16th Nov, with a free update for PS5 owners

It's now been confirmed God of War: Sons of Sparta, the mostly forgotten Metroidvania game that launched earlier this year, will indeed be ported back to PS4.

Having debuted on PS5 in February, the PS4 version launches next week, on 16th November 2026.

For both current PS5 owners and any new players on PS4, the base title will be supported by two extra modes: Hermes Mode and Erebus Mode.

Hermes Mode is a speedrun challenge featuring a split-based timer and a scoreboard. You automatically unlock the mode by finishing the game, or you can enter the following cheat code on the main menu to access it straight away:

Hermes Mode Code: Up Up Down Down Left Right Left Right L1 R1 Touch Pad

Then there's Erebus Mode, which revolves around both you and the enemy dying from one hit. It's dubbed the "ultimate challenge" for God of War: Sons of Sparta.

When it launched on PS5 following a shadow drop reveal, Sons of Sparta didn't exactly set the world alight. We enjoyed the adventure, awarding it a 7/10 score in our God of War: Sons of Sparta PS5 review.

"It's a mostly successful experiment; the Metroidvania structure works well with the franchise's mechanics, and it looks and sounds the part. However, it takes too long to really come into its own, leaving the early parts of the game feeling a bit lacking compared to the richer experience found later on."

We were one of the few who did, though, as the overall critic rating on Metacritic sits at a 64.

Now on a less powerful system, it's not like a PS4 version can fix any of its problems. At least it gives those people still using a PS4 a chance to play the game.

#4022. Path of Exile 2's 1.0 version is out this year after all, arriving in December with a full campaign, two neat new classes, and more

About a year ago, the devs behind Path of Exile 2 delayed the game's 1.0 release to an unspecified point in time, only offering the hope that it wouldn't slip into 2027 (doing much the same about half a year later). But there's good news: it won't! As the action RPG now has a 1.0 release date locked in, alongside a look at what you can expect when it arrives.

As shared by developer Grinding Gear Games, Path of Exile 2 will be launching into 1.0 next month on December 11th. Probably the biggest aspect of the update is the fact that the game's campaign will be completely playable, with the fifth and sixth acts being added in wrapping up the story that's been built up over its early access release. You'll also have two new classes to play around with, if you've gotten bored of the ones you've tried so far or just fancy something new.

The first is the Shadow, which appropriately introduces a stealth mechanic. As you might expect of such a class, while you're in stealth, "monsters can't see you until you get within a short distance of them." Being in said mode also bolsters your dagger with a range of bonuses, and the Shadow also has another weapon type available to them, traps. You prepare these in stealth, "then trigger them automatically as you strike. Traps explode in the order they were thrown, allowing you to set up the perfect combo!" And the other class is the Duelist, who has the new stance mechanic. This lets you strengthen your sword skills, "enhancing each of them in different ways," with various stances allowing for "even deadlier combinations."

Beyond that, there's a new league to try out that lets you team up with Varek and his mercs to "conquer Wraeclast!" A whole bunch of new items have been added in, with many being revamped, and you'll also find new skills gems and support gems reworked. The passive skill tree has also seen a makeover, and a number of classes have also received some improvements. You can read about all of that in more detail right here.

Rebel Wolves has "even more crazy ideas" up its sleeves

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

It was a bad time to be a vampire fan and enjoyer of video games until precisely September 2, 2026, when a team of CD Projekt Red veterans released The Blood of Dawnwalker, easily the best vampire game in years. Rebel Wolves didn't take home any awards at the Golden Joysticks this year, but it showed a lot of class by congratulating and paying respect to its competition, including Ultimate Game of the Year, Resident Evil Requiem. We caught up with Rebel Wolves founder and Blood of Dawnwalker game director Konrad Tomaszkiewicz at the Golden Joysticks, and his mood was celebratory.

"Many people told us the vampire genre is cursed somehow," Tomaszkiewicz says. "I think that we somehow lifted this curse. We have our own place in the genre also, with the narrative sandbox and hybrid combat and the other things we have, and it's great to have something like this because we already have ideas how to expand it and how to make even more crazy ideas in the game. I'm really happy because, for us, the development was a lot of fun."

It's definitely true that there's a stigma around vampire games in particular that's been hard to shake for, oh, I don't know, ever. The Castlevania series set an impossibly high standard going back to the '80s, and on second thought, may have inadvertently cursed the genre to be plagued by clunkers like Vampire Rain, Redfall, and most disappointingly, Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines 2. There have definitely been some moderate successes over the years; I liked Vampyr alright, and most recently Castlevania: Belmont's Curse has been a triumphant revival, but by and large vampire games really put the suck in I want to suck your blood.

The Blood of Dawnwalker isn't just an extraordinarily solid vampire game, it's also one of my favorite RPGs in recent memory, with The Witcher 3-caliber writing across its entire main quest and every side quest I've encountered. I'm not sure exactly what Tomaszkiewicz means when he says Rebel Wolves has expansion ideas, but the studio has confirmed a sequel is on the way.

6 things I need from The Blood of Dawnwalker's sequel

#4020. "This trailer is my way of saying goodbye": Have a listen to the Mass Effect 5 score that could have been, courtesy of one of the original games' composers

By this point I'm probably safe in assuming that you all know EA are shutting down BioWare, and that Mass Effect 5 has been cancelled in turn. You may have also seen that an internal trailer for Mass Effect 5, or Universe as it was seemingly going to be called, was leaked not long after the news broke, and that Sam Hulick, one of the composers on the original trilogy of games, shared he was going to offer up his re-scored version of the trailer. Well, it's N7 Day, as rough as that will be for many of the developers on the game, but Hulick has stood by his word, and shared an oral glimpse at what the world of Mass Effect Universe could have sounded like.

You can check out this new version of the trailer below, perhaps pop it on while you have a read of the rest of this post, as Hulick did also write in a Patreon blog about his experience with the series. "As part of my own closure, and as a love letter to the fans, I really wanted to re-score the leaked Mass Effect Universe trailer in time for N7 Day this year," he wrote. "BioWare edited a killer track called “Quartz” by French 79 to fit their trailer, which I think hinted at a slight directional shift in the score. Using that as inspiration, along with the musical tone from my work on the first three Mass Effect games, I hit the studio and got to work."

As it turns out, BioWare had actually reached out to Hulick asking him to potentially do some work for the project. "This year, BioWare emailed me asking if I was interested in working with them on an internal demo, and they said they were 'hoping to get some music written that would feel like Mass [Effect], supporting our new direction.' Of course, I said yes!" This doesn't mean he wouldn't have composed the actual game, as a composer hadn't been officially selected, but Hulick said he was "more than happy to collaborate on the new game’s musical direction and help make their internal demo sound as good as it could."

Hulick also spoke of some of the ideas he had for the direction Mass Effect Universe's soundtrack could take, noting how he "thought it would’ve been incredible to bring more songs with lyrics into the game," considering how many people loved the first game's end-credits song. "This would’ve been a great way to highlight more emotional moments in the narrative. Artists at the top of my collaboration list included Gunship, NINA, and The Midnight, all of whom have a moody, cinematic synthwave vibe that would’ve meshed well with the score in my head. And I’m pretty sure the Gunship guys are gamers, and if they’re Mass Effect fans, that would’ve been the icing on the cake!"

Of course, with the studio now closing, this never got to go very far, the news hitting Hulick "particularly hard, as the Mass Effect trilogy is a core part of my origin story as a composer." For the composer, ultimately "this trailer is my way of saying goodbye… at least for now." This continues to be a horrendously sad moment in the industry! As always, solidarity with the team at BioWare.

#4019. Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World details early adventure

Publisher and developer Square Enix, and developer TOSE have released new information and screenshots for Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World introducing protagonists Bianca and Nera‘s early adventure, Witherwood Castle, and the surrounding Witherwood region.

■ Explore a Strange World with a Team of Your Favorite Monsters!

Thursday, December 3, 2026, marks the simultaneous worldwide release date of Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World. Our protagonists on this adventure are none other than Bianca and Nera from Dragon Quest V: Hand of the Heavenly Bride. A mysterious fairy transports the girls to Witherwood, a kingdom in an unfamiliar world, where they hope to obtain some Leaves of Life that they believe will cure their sick fathers. However, Witherwood is beset by dark forces that have drained the land of its living energy, all but eradicating the Leaves of Life from existence. To ensure the Leaves of Life will grow once more, Bianca and Nera must become monster wranglers—plucky types with the power to befriend monsters—and lead their team of loyal allies on an adventure across this strange new world.

—Take your favorite monsters along with you as you explore all corners of the world. What new adventures await you beyond the curve of the horizon?

—You can now scout monsters on the fly as you explore, as well as in battle. It’s never been easier to befriend all the monsters you want!

—The Synthesis feature lets you combine two monsters to create a new one. You’ll have to synthesize many, many monsters on your quest to build a powerful party.

—It’s your job to rid the world of the evil forces that drain the land of its life energy.

■ The Early Adventure: Becoming a Monster Wrangler

Soon after arriving in Witherwood to look for the Leaves of Life, Bianca and Nera are given the power to befriend monsters and set out on their quest as fledgeling monster wranglers. Once you’ve decided which character you want to control and have your starting monster, it’s time for you to go off and befriend a few more!

—You can choose to begin the adventure as either Bianca or Nera. Each protagonist will find it easier to befriend monsters from different families, and their Wrangler’s Sprit ability provides different beneficial effects when it activates during battle. So, examine their differences and pick your favorite!

—After you answer Fluffy’s questions, he’ll present you with your first monster. The monster you get depends on your responses, but there’s no need to overthink things!

—When you enter battle, the monsters you’ve befriended will fight under your command. Give them specific orders or set their general tactics and march your way to victory!

—Use a Show of Force in battle to attempt to befriend an enemy monster. If you succeed, the monster will join your team. On rare occasions, a monster may even ask to join you of its own accord after a battle ends!

■ The Early Adventure: Witherwood Castle, Your Base of Operations

Witherwood Castle will soon become something of a home base for Bianca and Nera as their adventure ramps up. Conveniently, the castle town is home to many amenities that will serve the girls well on their quest.

The kingdom’s ruler, King Withers, holds court in his throne hall, from where he provides the girls with invaluable advice. See what he has to say if you find yourself at a loss for where to go next.

The paddock is where your monsters hang out when not in your party. From here, you can also access the monster depot when you want to make changes to your team line-up.

The item shop sells a range of wares, including meat, which monsters absolutely love! The stock changes as you progress through the story, so check back regularly to see what’s new.

As the story unfolds, you’ll start to see changes in Witherwood Castle and the adjoining town. For starters, a monster called Tony will appear and challenge you to complete scouting trials for a reward, and townsfolk will offer their monsters to you for synthesis in the form of matchmaking opportunities. Also, the accessories you can equip to your monsters can be upgraded at a workshop that will open after a while. Witherwood has plenty on offer to help our young wranglers strengthen their team in preparation for the next step of their adventure!

This odd monster will give you clues describing a very specific monster he wants you to show him. The trials get more difficult with each one you complete, but the rewards get better to match.

Some townsfolk will offer you their monsters to use for synthesis. You can contribute any monster you like, but if you can provide the one the townsperson mentions, you’ll be able to perform a special synthesis!

With the right crafting materials and enough gold, you can upgrade your accessories twice at most. You’ll find these materials when you’re out exploring, but monsters sometimes drop them after battle as well.

■ The Early Adventure: Exploring the Witherwood Region

Once all the preparations are complete, it’s time to start exploring the game’s first main area: Witherwood! The region is divided into several sub-areas, each with its own distinct vibe and unique changes that occur as the day shifts to night. With Roots of Creation and Lifebuds to locate, as well as super-strong monsters and dungeons to discover, every area is worth exploring to its fullest.

Each area is home to monsters that may disappear or behave differently as day becomes night. For example, the teenie sanguini is strictly nocturnal, meaning you’ll find a different monster if you return to the same place during the daytime.

What to Do With the Withered Roots of Creation and Lifebuds?

—Give a Root of Creation a sprinkle with the Waterwing Can to revive it. Doing so will add it to the Zoom list for fast travel and create a one-stop-shop for healing monsters, adjusting your party, synthesizing, and changing the time.

—Helping the Lifebuds to bloom will provide your party with permanent passive boosts, such as increased experience points, that will really benefit you. If you see a Lifebud, be sure to give it a drink!

The monsters you see stomping about with a red aura around them are incredibly powerful. You can try fighting them at the start of the game if you really want, but it’s advised to wait until you have a stronger team.

While dungeons are home to hordes of monsters, they also contain valuable treasures, like mini medals that you can exchange for superb prizes at the Mini Medal Swap Swap in Witherwood.

In the depths of a dungeon, a ferocious monster often lies in wait. But before you jump into battle, it’s a good idea to head to a nearby Root of Creation to heal up and prepare your party.

■ The Early Adventure: Strengthen Your Team and Head to the Next Region

Before they can start synthesizing, Bianca and Nera must team up to take down a massive monster in a Joint Battle, as well as emerge victorious at the Battle Arena. But you can’t just synthesize with any old riffraff—you’ll need two monsters at Level 10 or above in order to synthesize a new one. With enough battles under your belt and a few strong monsters synthesized, you’ll be ready to explore the next region: Pays de l’Oseille!

Team Up to Beat the Massive Monster Enorman

—If you’re controlling Bianca for the Joint Battle, she’ll command your main party, with Nera in charge of your reserves—and vice versa if you’re using Nera.

—When a massive monster becomes enraged, each of its attacks will deal heavy damage, but it’ll be more susceptible to damage itself. Keep calm and use the opportunity to attack!

If you find the Battle Arena to be tough going, try leveling up your party and including some monsters in your team that can use spells or healing abilities.

With Both Trials Done, Go to the Starry Shine in the Castle to Start Synthesizing

—If you have two monsters at Level 10 or higher, you can combine them to synthesize a new one. You can even synthesize monsters from any Root of Creation you find out in the wider world.

—Child monsters born through synthesis can inherit the Talents of their parents. Some monsters can only be made through synthesis, so try to explore as many combinations as you can.

A number of regions beyond Witherwood are waiting to be explored. Hunting for treasure in a sunken shipwreck, adventuring among giant fruits and veggies, and many more adventures await you!

Bianca and Nera’s search for the Leaves of Life is only just beginning!

Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World is due out for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series, Switch 2, Switch, and PC via Steam and Microsoft Store on December 3. A demo is available now.

#4018. County of Fortune, now out in early access, is a medieval city builder that asks, why limit yourself to just one city?

Don't count your towns before they've hatched

I know what you want. The humble city builder isn't enough for you any more, is it? You need a cities builder, you can't just stop at one, but you don't want to build up an entirely different city on a new save file. If it were up to you, they'd all be on the same map, a motorway's worth of a drive away from each other. If we're talking contemporary cities, I can't help you, but if you can settle for numerous medieval towns across an entire county, then County of Fortune should do just fine.

County of Fortune just landed in early access a couple of days ago, and as mentioned (and as the name suggests), you're building up an entire county! "You place whole settlements across the county and lay each one out on a medieval grid. Each one grows, specializes, and knits into a living region where rivers and resources decide what thrives," the game's Steam page explains. "As the county matures, a second game begins. Named mayors run each settlement. Rival noble houses weave politics across the region. And migrating cultures bless some villages, while complicating others."

To start with, it's up to you where you want to place each of your settlements, deciding how they individually function as you do. The towns are then partially procedurally generated as they get built up, slowly connecting to other nearby towns. "The scale is the point. You are not zooming into a single town - you are zooming out to see a whole county come to life." A big part of the strategy comes down to how you navigate the map; finding resource deposits, picking appropriate terrain profiles, utilising rivers efficiently, finding a good climate, setting good trade routes, it's all about working with the land you've got.

Each settlement will produce different things depending on the materials available to them in close proximity, meaning each one has a unique function. You've got different types of characters to consider too: mayors, noble houses and cultures, all intersecting with different elements of how a town functions. Seems like a unique approach to city building! And as mentioned, it's out in early access; you can pick it up on Steam here.

#4017. PSA: GTA 6 Does Not Have Online Multiplayer at Launch

GTA 6 is now less than a week away from its official launch, coming to PS5 on 19th November, 2026.

It's likely to become the biggest entertainment launch of all time, with excitement at a fever pitch coming off the back of GTA 5, which is the third best-selling game ever at a staggering 235 million copies.

Something that not everyone may know, however, is that GTA 6 will be a single-player game only at first; the online component will not be available initially.

This won't come as a shock to those in the know, as Rockstar Games has described it as a solo experience and has not yet referred to any form of online play.

However, it seems there are many expectant fans that are excited to hop straight into multiplayer with their buddies. In case you didn't know, you won't be able to do this when GTA 6 launches next week.

I suspect this confusion comes from just how long GTA 5 has been around. The game was first released on PS3 13 years ago, and GTA Online is almost as old, launching a couple of weeks after the main game.

Re-releases of GTA 5 on PS4 and PS5 have always arrived with GTA Online as part of the package, so even though the original game didn't have online multiplayer to begin with, it's been a constant presence for millions of players for well over a decade.

It makes sense that people have become accustomed to GTA 5 providing GTA Online, and took it for granted that its sequel would include the feature from day one. This is not the case.

For GTA 6, it's expected that an updated version of GTA Online will launch sometime in 2027, though an exact date has yet to be confirmed. It won't take a full year to appear, despite what this recent Bloomberg video inadvertently suggests.

It's believed that GTA Online will come to GTA 6 in a matter of a few months, possibly launching in the first quarter of 2027.

Rumour has it that the PC port of GTA 6 will launch in a similar timeframe, and it would make sense for these two things to be aligned.

So, to summarise: GTA 6 does not feature online multiplayer at launch, but it likely won't be too far off.

Mega Crit expects "to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready" for the main game

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Slay the Spire 2's early access journey continues, and developer Mega Crit isn't skimping on what it's calling the roguelike deckbuilder's "biggest update yet." Update v0.113.0 goes into beta today, introducing a new character in The Fool. It also adds two new game modes, called Blitz and Dread.

"Wah!! The first new character for Early Access arrives," Mega Crit enthuses in the patch notes. "A silly musician who wields a bow! How can such a whimsical creature survive within the Spire? Why, that's up to you! We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch. Even more importantly, be sure to have fun figuring out all the strategies and story of this gently bard. It would be foolish not to!"

If you want to opt into the beta branch and check out The Fool before the character is ready for the main game, just hop into the game's properties on Steam, go into the Game Versions & Betas tab, and select "public-beta" from the dropdown menu.

On top of the new character, there are two new game modes Blitz is "condensed and chaotic deckbuilding-focused mode" where the "Merchant's wares feel a bit off, the map is gone, and Gold no longer matters." Dread is a "brutally difficult mode" that requires you to reach Ascension on every character – including the Fool – to even take a run at.

A few months ago, Mega Crit said it was slowing down on updates so it could focus on "bigger, more impactful content," and it looks like we're starting to see the fruits of that pivot. Slay the Spire 2 launched back in March, and expect the game's early access period to be similar to the year-and-a-half it took the previous game to reach version 1.0, so it looks like we've got a fair few more updates to look forward to in the meantime.

#4015. Echoes of Mirror's Edge, Dishonored and a dream set in Italy I once had can be found in Boars in Rome, an expressive parkour platformer set in dystopian Rome

Years ago, I had this dream where I was parkouring through a greatly sunken version of Venice, no doubt sourced from the many hours I put into Assassin's Creed 2 as a teen who should have been studying for their GCSEs a lot more than they were. It's stuck with me after all this time mostly because of how much I wanted to capture that feeling again somehow, as the real Assassin's Creed didn't quite cut it. And lo and behold, there I was today browsing Bluesky when I came across Boars in Rome, a Mirror's Edge and Counter Strike Surf inspired parkour platformer set in a dystopian version of Rome.

Truthfully, witnessing the clip I've shared below was baffling to me. "This is what I dreamt of!" More or less, anyway, for the setting isn't quite the same; "You have been selected to start a new life off planet. Earth has been abandoned," explains the game's Steam page. "Machines keep working and nature claims what remains. Find out what happened while you were frozen in time by exploring the remnants of Rome where historical monuments mix with futurist megastructures."

Mirrors Edge x Counter Strike Surf where you parkour on anything! Be smooth n stylish in dystopian Rome. Or just jump around and explore, whatever works for you. It's called Boars in Rome! #PitchYaGame[image or embed]

Not all of it matches that dream of mine, some of it leans much more into brutalism than the typical, much older architecture you'd expect of Rome, but it's there nonetheless. In motion, Boars in Rome feels quite oneiric too. There is so much more control over the game's avatar than what my real body is capable of, or wants to do. You can run, jump, slide and wallrun, positioning it quite closely to VHOLUME mechanically. Where it differs is in its additives, movement tech like being able to swing on lampposts or vault over low down obstacles.

VHOLUME is more of a game about providing you with a simple toolkit and leaving you to push it to its maximum. Boars in Roam is a touch more expressive, and I'd dare to even call it an immersive sim. The levels you can romp around are linear, you have an end point to reach, only the journey is up to you. It certainly feels appropriate to put it in the im sim camp given that, at least the game's first level, calls to mind Viktor Antonov's work on Dishonored (and Half-Life 2, too, honestly).

As it currently stands, there's no release date for Boars in Rome, but there is a playtest you can sign up and gain immediate access to if you fancy a go yourself; you can do so on Steam right here, or at least pop it a wishlist.

#4013. The Sunday Papers

The Sunday Papers is our weekly roundup of great writing about (mostly) videogames from across the web.

Sundays are for waking up covered in sand. The roof of your house is missing. A small man stands in the emptied bed of a dump truck. "You know, everybody's always asking about Elder Scrolls 6," he says. "You know, everybody's always asking about Elder Scrolls 6," he repeats. "You know, everybody's always asking about Elder Scrolls 6," he declares once again, beginning to move towards you this time. "You know, everybody's always asking about Elder Scrolls 6." You realise your hands are tied down. Oh no.

Is he about to sit on your face? WAIT, THAT'S NOW ILLEGAL HERE IN THE UK. NO, PLEASE, DON'T SIT ON MY-time seems to slow as the bare backside approaches your visage. As its cheeks prepare to become as sandy as yours, you hear its wielder say: "And we thought, hey, given the moment..."

Panicking, you scrabble for anything to say which might free you before something that might get a British MP's hackles up can occur. "Things first went awry when I turned up for my appointment to find a tall German man wearing a cowboy hat asking a PR if he could play the game," you blurt out. The posterior momentarily stops moving towards you. Buoyed, you continue to tell a story you heard from VGC's Chris Scullion.

I was asked if I minded sharing my one-to-one appointment with this chap too, to which my inherent British cowardly courtesy kicked in and I lied that it was perfectly fine.

"I want drums", he said as he entered the room. "We are playing Dani California by Red Hot Chili Peppers." Rather than ask him whether he also fancied telling me where I was going for dinner later, I picked up my guitar and went along with it, eager to just play the game.

The bottom begins its agonising crawl towards your kisser once more. You can feel the occupants of parliamentary benches begin to sense a disturbance in the force. Maybe if you can make the bumholder sad, that'll do the trick. You try to remember how Sebastian Cardoso of Game Studio Unlocked's presentation on the tragic fates of game studios after acquisitions went.

A hundred and twenty-three of the 362 developers were shut outright. The average life from acquisition to closure is 6.4 years and the median is 5, meaning half of all closed studios were dead within five years of their acquisition.

The familiar names mostly died fast. EA closed Pandemic two years after buying it. Sony shut Firewalk barely a year and a half in. Warner Bros. closed Player First roughly seven months after acquiring it. Bluepoint, closed at the five-year mark, is exactly what the median looks like.

It's no use. That arse's shadow its creeping across ever more of your face like your're a planet with a nose and it's the Vogon Constructor Fleet. Maybe you can somehow contort your head to the side. Arrrggghh. You call on all the strength of muscles you barely ever use and think of the incredible gymnastic feats executed by Physical Contortion Gamer's Josh Wolens during an ongoing GTA diary series.

Attempting to do flips, then, just sort of rotates your entire body below the diaphragm while your head and chest area remain bolt upright, rigid in such a way that you could feasibly fly a flag from your own thorax.

Which looks odd. Nevertheless, it is pretty fun to scoot and roll your way through Los Santos. At one point, I attempted a double frontflip in the middle of a part of the map that had been deleted for some reason. It didn't quite work out, and I ended up colliding with and possibly killing a man in a fursuit.

It doesn't work. You can't get away. You begin to scream. The posterioperator stops repeating the words "You know, everybody's always asking about Elder Scrolls 6". Instead, he asks where that mysterious German cowboy you mentioned earlier has gone. You don't have a clue, and can't help admitting as much. "Ah well." The derriere resumes its descent, now mere inches from your mug. This is the end. You have one last rummage through your mind for possible solutions.

Respec's Tom Orry hasn't managed to save you. "Fine, sit on my face and send me to hell," you shout into the pinkish ring of doom as British cops prepare to ram-raid your abode and arrest you for crimes against a prude's definition of acceptable shagging.

The bum stops. Its owner asks if you've just said the word Sentinel. "Yes," you lie.

The arse is raised and swapped for the face of a man. "What a perfect time for you to realise what The Elder Scrolls 6 is actually called," he says.

You notice he's not Todd Howard. Or Adrian Edmondson.

"It's Ade's month off and they needed another baldy to play this esteemed role," Sir Patrick Stewart announces, clearly responding the look of befuddlement your face can still have since it hasn't been crushed by a ten-tonne tush. You wonder how you didn't recognise his voice before, especially given he played the emperor in Oblivion.

"Here's to the next Bethesda game after Starfield," the Stew sings as the police bust through the door and he's beamed up before they can tackle him.

25 OG Xbox titles are now on PC, and it's an utterly bizarre list of games

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

This weekend marks Xbox's 25th birthday, and while any celebration of the milestone is going to be muted in view of the layoff bloodbath Microsoft is currently engaging in, the gaming division is taking steps to keep us thinking about the brand in a positive light. That includes a fresh expansion to the list of original Xbox games that are now backwards compatible on PC.

After the four original Xbox games that Microsoft brought to PC earlier this year, another 21 have joined the list – a total of 25 games for the console's 25th birthday. The new list of games is an utterly bizarre one, largely dominated by LucasArts titles. That includes plenty of beloved Star Wars titles, alongside largely forgotten obscurities like Secret Weapons Over Normandy and Thrillville.

Some of the titles you might recognize, like Star Wars classics Battlefront 2, Jedi Outcast, and Knights of the Old Republic, are odd choices in themselves, since those games are already available on PC. Assuming Xbox is using the same emulation-based solution to port these games, they're all going to be substantially worse experiences than simply picking up the native PC versions for the same price on Steam.

That goes double for The Elder Scrolls 3: Morrowind, which is also on the list of newly added games. The Xbox version of Morrowind was a stunning technical achievement back in 2002, but it was notoriously janky even at the time, filled with bugs and technical limitations that have been robustly addressed on PC. I struggle to come up with a compelling reason anyone would want to play this version over the PC original today, especially with all the mods available for the RPG.

There are two games I absolutely will not complain about, however: TimeSplitters 2 and TimeSplitters: Future Perfect. Developed by the Rare veterans at Free Radical Design, the TimeSplitters series was a spiritual successor to classic N64 games GoldenEye and Perfect Dark, refreshing the FPS gameplay for a new generation with fun weapon gimmicks and charmingly goofy characters.

TimeSplitters never moved beyond cult classic status, and attempts to revive the series ended in failure. None of these games ever got PC ports, which makes their inclusion arguably the most notable part of this Xbox backwards compatibility update.

Id Software devs laid off by Microsoft form their own studio and don't hold back in their announcement: "It really felt like an attack"

His love for games was sparked somewhere between Metal Gear Solid 2 and Knights of the Old Republic, and these days you can usually find him splitting his entertainment time between retro gaming, the latest big action-adventure title, or a long haul in American Truck Simulator.

#4011. Ahead of The Witcher 3: Songs of the Past, here's a "lore friendly unofficial expansion to Geralt's life in Toussaint" from a well-established quest modder

While its remastered upgrade might have broken cover in late September, The Witcher 3's extra expansion isn't set to join it until next year. With 2027 still a month and a bit away, a modder's taken it upon themselves to add a few more adventures to Geralt's time in Toussaint, Blood and Wine's gorgeous French-ish duchy, before the bloke from the river heads off to Letten for Songs of the Past.

So far, only the opening chapter of the mod - Annals of the Duchy - has been released. It adds in a new quest about Geralt, with help from either Yen or Triss if either have made the trip out to Toussaint as part of your playthrough, getting into a scrape thanks to a halfling who seems to promise Gerry the chance to juice up his vineyard's vines.

The mod's creator, Jontej, has previously put together a couple of other custom Witcher 3 quests. While they do look to have used AI voices in English versions of those mods, for Annals of the Duchy they've enlisted a cast of human actors for both Enlish and Polish versions.

Jontej has plans to expand this new questline going forwards, having cited specific "plans for an extra storyline involving Syanna", whom you might remember from Blood and Wine's main quest. Given that - spoilers ahead - the mod relies on you having gotten the Blood and Wine ending which sees both Anna Henrietta and Syanna survive, as well as having paid to renovate the gardens of Geralt's vineyard. They add that, when it comes to their additions, the "timeline fits quite well [with] the upcoming official Songs of the Past Expansion, which has been confirmed to take place after the events of the main game/Blood and Wine".

As much as I've argued that, as of right now, I struggle to see how Songs of the Past will manage to outdo Blood and Wine as a satisfying end to Geralt's tale in the Witcher game trilogy, I am intrigued by the idea of a few more modded adventures showing Gerry adjusting to the semi-retired life. After all, Toussaint's got to have a few more dungeons tucked away that're worth temporarily dusting off the White Wolf's twin swords for.

To kick off Annals of the Duchy, you'll need to trigger its first quest by taking a stroll from the Corvo Bianco manor house down to its gardens between 11am and 1pm. It's worth noting that any other mod which messes with Yen, Triss or companions in general has a chance to muck things up as far as Jontej's creation goes.

#4010. Indie game website itch.io expands its AI disclosure filter as 'AI slop' continues to overwhelm Steam and other storefronts

Indie game storefront itch.io has expanded its AI disclosure filters, allowing its users to better separate games made with the controversial technology from those who don't.

This expansion, revealed on its official BlueSky account, includes Itchio's search page which now features a "No AI" box. By ticking this, users can hide any game on the website that features the generative AI disclosure. Games created using generative AI must have this disclosure to be present on the platform, similarly to Steam, although without an option to describe to what extent the tech was used.

This change comes shortly after itch.io also revealed the number of game pages being made on the website each day had doubled in the past two months. And, of course, the number of games downloaded and purchases have not doubled to match this new supply.

itch.io is also facing issues linked to the sheer file size. The storefront has a terms of service policy against AI spam, which it cited shortly after it publicly announced "a couple terabytes of AI slop" had been deleted.

This change comes as the industry as a whole has been clogged with an influx of AI games. Steam Next Fest had a record-breaking number of demo submissions last month. Developers pulled demos in fear of their game being copied, and with Steam saying it's the developer's responsibility to make their games less copyable.

It's an issue that isn't going away any time soon. Even as Claude creator Anthropic has introduced rules preventing unoriginal game clones, alternative AI tools can still be used to create them, and the process of creating games using AI tools will still allow for hastily made, low effort slop. Perhaps filters, like the one itch.io has expanded, is a workable solution to this on-going problem.

#4007. Rockstar were "definitely" thinking about giving a Japanese studio the keys to GTA, says former tech director - "I have a name, but I'm not gonna say it"

Obbe Vermeij on ancient plans for a GTA Tokyo

Since time immemorial, North American and European publishers have racked their brains over ways to make their games sell in Japan, ancient heartland of mythical beings like Mario, Sonic, and Polaroid Pete. In the late noughties, Microsoft launched a big push to give Japanese youth the Xbox virus with such targeted console exclusives as Blue Dragon and Lost Odyssey. And Rockstar once dreamed of making a Grand Theft Auto game set in Tokyo.

Speaking to me last week, Rockstar North's former technical director Obbe Vermeij shared a little about the abandoned project. Emphasis on the "little" – it doesn't appear to have gotten very far, despite recently unearthed allusions to "Tokyo PS2" in GTA 5's source code.

Rockstar's parent company Take-Two Interactive filed a trademark for GTA Tokyo back in 2003, the year before the release of the Los Angeles-flavoured GTA: San Andreas. At the time, Rockstar were apparently looking at collaborating with a Japanese studio on the project. "So this was kind above my pay grade," Vermeij told me. "But yeah, there were negotiations with studios, and I have a name, but I'm not gonna say it, because then it becomes like a bigger thing than it is, and I'll probably get it wrong, and I don't know how far the negotiations were, how serious it was. I mean, it was definitely serious. It was the plan. But I don't know how close it got to actually happening."

The game itself would likely have been a contemporary story, not a historical yarn like Rockstar's subsequent Red Dead Redemption. "It definitely had samurai swords in it, I remember that, but I think it was present-day probably," Vermeij went on. "Or sort of not too [far off] - it wasn't, like, sort of the medieval era in Japanese history, or anything. It was definitely not like that."

Vermeij was at Rockstar from 1995 to 2009, where he worked on the first four mainline 3D GTA games, plus some handheld spin-offs. During that time, he says, Rockstar frequently considered the idea of a Grand Theft Auto set outside the United States. "In the same way that we were always thinking about other games, we also thought about cities that would be cool, and it was always the same list," he said. "It was Moscow, London. Istanbul, Rio de Janeiro, maybe Paris and Tokyo. It was always the same ones that people suggested."

Grand Theft Auto has never quite the money-spinner in Japan that it is in North America and Europe. Localised editions of the original three 3D GTA games were published by Capcom, sometime after the original releases, selling a few hundred thousand copies apiece in their launch years.

"I think perhaps [Rockstar's co-founders] the Housers were a little annoyed that GTA wasn't as big in Japan as they thought it deserved to be," Vermeij reflected. "So it kind of made sense to get a local studio to do it. Japanese people actually kind of like different games from westerners a fair bit. For instance, they don't like first person shooters and stuff. So, it made sense to have a Japanese studio have a shot at it, and I think it would have been really cool, because you know, a GTA made by somebody else in Japanese culture – that's something I would probably play."

Take-Two ultimately abandoned their original "GTA Tokyo" trademark in 2008. It's not clear how much Rockstar have considered setting GTA overseas since Vermeij's day, but co-founder Dan Houser (who left the company in 2020) recently told podcaster Lex Fridman that they ultimately decided it wasn't a credible objective.

“We made a little thing in London 26 years ago - GTA London - for the top-down for PS1," he said. "That was pretty cute and fun, as the first mission pack ever for PlayStation 1. I think for a full GTA game, we always decided there was so much Americana inherent in the IP, it would be really hard to make it work in London or anywhere else. You know, you needed guns, you needed these larger-than-life characters. It just felt like the game was so much about America, possibly from an outsider's perspective. But that was so much about what the thing was that it wouldn't really have worked in the same way elsewhere.”

If this article has left you pining for the Shibuya Scramble NPC-tipping sim that will never be, I bring good news: Japanese developers are quite capable of making their own urban open worlders. The obvious go-tos are Sega's Yakuza/Like A Dragon games, with their abundance of lovingly modelled eateries and discount stores. There's also Ghostwire: Tokyo, a respectable first-person parkour sim, though this particular incarnation of Tokyo has a lot of paranormal congestion. All these games have the advantage of being playable on PC right now. As for GTA 6? Who can say, but Vermeij thinks Rockstar might want to port it sooner to get ahead of the slopcomp craze.

#4006. COD: Modern Warfare 4 DMZ patch has nerfed UAV Towers so you're not immediately visible everywhere you go

The Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 patches continue, with the latest delivering some big changes to the game's extraction mode DMZ. The latest hotfix introduced a key balance change to one of DMZ's most controversial mechanics: UAV Towers.

UAV Towers, previously guaranteed to spawn in every Point of Interest (POI) in the map, have now had their spawn logic randomised. Infinity Ward also reduced their spawn rate by 40 percent, meaning you're less likely to find them across the various regions of the map. As noted in the patch notes, that change also prevents multiple towers from spawning the same area. The only exception is the Deadtown area, which factors into DMZ Order progression and requires multiple towers.

By taking away the guarantee that each POI will have at least one UAV Tower, the patch removes one of the core tactics PvP-inclined and aggressive players have been relying on since DMZ's launch. It's common for players to spawn in, and immediately run around activating as many UAV Towers as possible to reveal the movement of enemy players, even if they're not interested in directly engaging them.

Indeed, some of the UAV Towers cover extraction areas, so it's easy for players intending to ruin the day of others as they're extracting to set up elaborate traps. Making matters worse, a particular character trait prevents UAV Towers from expiring, allowing the scans to stay up for the entire match.

Infinity Ward has not commented directly on that trait, but the developer confirmed it's being changed so the Sedative Inhaler - which hides you from UAVs - also works with those trait-upgraded towers, though that change won't arrive until sometime in Season 1.

Finally, today's update further makes it easier to stay undetected by boosting the Sedative Inhaler's duration to 120 seconds, double that of the previous 60, which should help while we wait for larger changes to be implemented.

DMZ has been one of Modern Warfare 4's most discussed modes online. Recently, players discovered what appears to be a separate matchmaking pool for Story Missions that prevents solo sessions from featuring other players, though with some caveats.

Playground Games is ramping up its marketing efforts for its upcoming Fable revival, and a new gameplay showcase seems to confirm the return of enemy Nymphs, which we haven't seen since the original Fable back in 2004.

The new Official Quest Gameplay trailer, released as part of Xbox's 25th anniversary shenanigans, shows a darker side to Albion than we're used to seeing, and I mean that literally. After cranking up the brightness on my monitor, I could see that the footage shows a female hero character seeking out her village's mysterious assailant with the help of a character named Arden. Tracing the attacker's path leads the duo through a heavily wooded forest with giant thorny vines and eventually, a confrontation with some familiar-looking foes outside a cave entrance.

Again, everything is dark in this trailer, but from what I can tell these fellas look a whole lot like the Wood Nymphs, which are one of two species of fairy-like creatures, the other being Water Nymphs, from OG Fable back in the day. They're referred to as "cursed monsters" in the quest log, but c'mon, those are fairies. They're little magical winged humanoids with big heads and tree bark-like skin, and they flutter around in clouds of colorful orbs and shoot ethereal projectiles your way. If that isn't a Wood Nymph, well then I don't know what a Wood Nymph is. And believe me, I know a thing or two about Wood Nymphs.

Anyway, otherwise the trailer is fairly unremarkable. Not in a bad way, just in a way that doesn't reveal anything super new or exciting to talk about, which makes sense considering we're just a few short months away from getting to play the game. Fable is out on PS5, Xbox Series X, and PC on February 23.

#4004. The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel is confirmed, finally getting new trailer and full name, 8 years, 4 months, and 23 days after its reveal

Today, Xbox and Bethesda have finally revealed the name and more information about The Elder Scrolls 6. The game, which we now know carries the subtitle Sentinel, was revealed in a special video that took place today, 3rd November 2026, almost exactly 15 years since the launch of The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim and eight years, four months, and 23 days since the first reveal of the title card for The Elder Scrolls 6. That's over 100 months, by the way, or 3067 days, if you want to get specific.

In the trailer, a glimpse of the new game - mostly with some fancy sand physics - before the name, Sentinel, is revealed formally. "The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes. A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate," says a quote in the video, attributed to Yazar, Moth Priest of High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell.

"For 40 years, we've explored new worlds, told unforgettable stories, and gone on incredible adventures together," says a blurb for new video. "From everyone at Bethesda Game Studios, thank you for joining us along this journey, for making these worlds your own, and for inspiring us to keep creating. Here's to 40 more."

This reveal comes after a report last week suggested we'd be seeing more of the highly-anticipated fantasy RPG in November, and which also predicted the name of the game. That report suggested that the title will take place in the Tamriel region of Hammerfell, will touch on the "history of the Elder Scrolls" and will "help uncover the secrets of these mysterious ancient artifacts". This trailer seems to confirm all that.

Asha Sharma, CEO of Xbox, said she'd played the game in August on a trip to the Bethesda offices, as a giant inflatable rat and a union protest took place outside. Notably, the reveal of the game is taking place not six months after Bethesda suffered sweeping job cuts (alongside many other Microsoft-owned studios) as part of Xbox's "reset".

So why has it taken eight years for Bethesda to show us this game? Previously, Skyrim's lead designer Bruce Nesmith noted that the studio and boss Todd Howard felt pressured to reveal the game to the world because "the pitchforks and torches were out". "[...] Todd's opinion - one which I share, by the way - is that the video game industry has short memories," he said in an interview in 2023. "Those companies that start touting their games years ahead of time, actually, you know, they screw themselves. The best time to start talking about it is six months before release." It's worth noting, then, that this is what Bethesda did with Fallout 4.

Does that hint at a timeline for more Sentinel footage being shown soon, and a potentially sooner-than-we-thought release date? Who knows. If we are going to see the game again anytime soon, it's most likely going to be during The Game Awards 2026, which is taking place on 10th December.
